Cyber Attack Disrupts Ecuador’s Payment Networks and Infrastructure; Economic Activity Hit Nationwide

A widespread cyber attack targeting Ecuador’s national infrastructure has severely disrupted digital payment systems, telecommunications, and power distribution across the country, government officials confirmed Thursday. The incident, which began early Wednesday and is ongoing, has affected a broad range of sectors, with Consorcio Shushufindi SA among the companies reporting operational difficulties.

The attack, believed to involve sophisticated ransomware, crippled several major payment gateways and caused outages in cellular and internet services in Quito, Guayaquil, and Cuenca. The Ministry of Telecommunications said in a statement that teams were “working nonstop to restore connectivity and secure critical systems,” but warned that recovery would be “gradual and may take several days.”

Many businesses and consumers are unable to process electronic transactions, leading to long lines at ATMs and a surge in cash withdrawals. “Payment terminals across the city have stopped working. We’re operating almost entirely in cash,” said Andrea Torres, manager of the Quito-based retailer Alimentos Andinos. The Association of Private Banks of Ecuador urged customers to limit nonessential banking and avoid panic withdrawals.

Consorcio Shushufindi SA, a key player in Ecuador’s energy sector, reported disruptions in its communication networks and delays in supply chain coordination. “Our operations have experienced significant slowdowns due to the attack on national infrastructure. We are prioritizing safety and working closely with authorities,” a company spokesperson told reporters.

The National Chamber of Commerce estimated that retail sales volumes fell by as much as 40% on Thursday, as electronic payments stalled and power outages forced closures in several regions. Industrial production in affected cities is also running below capacity.

Energy sector officials said that while the national grid remains stable, some localized power distribution systems were compromised, causing intermittent blackouts in coastal and Amazon regions. Port operators in Guayaquil reported cargo processing delays due to network outages.

“Ecuador’s reliance on digital infrastructure for commerce and logistics is now starkly evident,” said economic analyst Camilo Jaramillo. “A prolonged disruption could have a material impact on GDP growth projections for the quarter.”

Authorities are coordinating with international cybersecurity agencies as the attack continues. No group has claimed responsibility at this time.
